newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-UK clothing boom to boost Burton.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-UK clothing boom to boost Burton.

text.p: Strong clothing sales and an improvement in gross margins are expected to smarten up profits at Burton Group Plc, which reports annual results next Thursday.

The retailer, owner of Debenhams department stores and fashion outlets like Top Shop and Dorothy Perkins, is forecast to make full year profits of around 144 million stg against 93.1 million last time. The dividend is expected to rise to about 2.65 pence from 2.2 pence a share.
Buoyant consumer spending and a cool autumn has helped clothing sales, and Burton is likely to have benefitted from the upturn in demand.
The group has achieved a major turnaround, after over-expansion in the 1980s left it struggling in the early 1990s. Analysts say the pace of recovery might slow, but there is still more to come.
"There's more to go for," said one retail analyst who recommended buying the shares. "We can expect continued growth in margins but at a slower pace than in the past couple of years."

Burton has succeeded in moving away from excessive mark downs to drive sales and is improving margins by promoting higher margin own-label brands. In addition, the full benefits from rationalisation of suppliers and distribution reorganisation are still to come through, analysts said.
In July, Burton said gross margin rose by 2.1 percentage points in the 19 weeks to July 13.

Analysts were less enthusiastic about Burton's move into home shopping via the purchase of Innovations and Racing Green. These were seen as having long term potential but could push up costs in the short term, analysts said.
